title: pilot-data-escrow-retention-guidelines
body:
Purpose:
This is a workshop-output + engineering checklist for customer pilot (POC) setups that need a data escrow-style approach and pragmatic retention controls. Audience: SEs running pilots, infra engineers implementing ingestion, and legal/regulatory reviewers drafting lightweight DPA addenda for trials.

Scope and assumptions:
- Covers hosted and dedicated POC modes (not full private on-prem installs).
- Focus on short-lived trial data: transcripts, prompt/response pairs, debug traces, and infra logs.
- Goal: minimize risk while keeping enough telemetry for troubleshooting and quality monitoring.
- Not a final legal DPA; intended to provide recommended clauses and implementation patterns for customer review.

Customer scenario (example):
- Enterprise customer wants a 30-day pilot using hosted inference.
- They require: (a) no retention of raw PII beyond 7 days, (b) ability to escrow redacted transcripts for audit, (c) assurance that debug-level logs are not retained offsite.

Retention tiers (recommended):
- Tier 0 — Ephemeral request buffer: 0–7 days. Raw request/response pairs live in an encrypted S3 prefix for up to 7 days to support immediate troubleshooting. Access restricted to SE on-call.
- Tier 1 — Escrowed redacted set: 30–90 days (customer-selectable). Redacted transcripts, with deterministic redaction hashes, stored in a customer-scoped escrow bucket for audits.
- Tier 2 — Aggregated metrics: indefinite/longer-term. Token counts, latency percentiles, error rates aggregated and stored without raw text.
- Tier 3 — Forensics only: snapshots taken only with customer approval and logged in ticketing system.

Technical controls (implementation checklist):
- Ingestion pipeline:
  - Route POC requests to a customer-specific S3 prefix: s3://redwood-pocs/{customer-id}/{env}/raw/
  - Apply server-side encryption (AES-256) and bucket policy locking: deny public ACLs.
  - Add lifecycle rule to expire "raw/" prefix after 7 days; transition to Glacier only after escrow threshold met.
- Redaction automation:
  - Run a staged scrubber job (open-source telemetry-scrub) before any long-term storage.
  - Redaction steps: PII regex (email, phone, SSNs), name entity tagging (NER), token-level hash replace for exact-match repeats.
  - Keep a mapping table of hash->redacted placeholder only in ephemeral KV and rotate keys weekly.
- KV / prefix cache handling (LLM-specific):
  - Disable persistent cache writes for POC unless customer requires.
  - If KV saved for performance testing, TTL=24–72h and stored in isolated per-customer Redis instance with automatic eviction.
- Logs & traces:
  - Default: set application log level to INFO for POCs; DEBUG off.
  - Remove or redaction-filter stack traces that contain request payloads before shipping to central logging.
  - Only send anonymized trace ids and metrics to third-party observability tools.
- Access controls & auditing:
  - Restrict S3 access to a short list of SE/Infra roles; enable MFA-delete where supported.
  - Require Jira ticket linkage for any manual retention extension (ticket ID in S3 object metadata).
  - Enable object-level logging for write/delete operations and store in an audit-only bucket with 1-year retention.

Sample DPA addendum language (boilerplate for POC):
--- Begin suggested clause ---
POC Data Handling and Retention Addendum
1. Definitions: "POC Data" means all customer-supplied prompts, model responses, debug traces, and ancillary telemetry generated during the trial period.
2. Retention: Provider will retain POC Data in raw form for a maximum of seven (7) calendar days from ingestion unless Customer explicitly requests retention in writing.
3. Escrowed Redacted Copy: Upon Customer request, Provider will produce and store a redacted copy of POC Data for up to thirty (30) days in a customer-dedicated escrow repository. Redaction will remove or hash PII as agreed.
4. Access & Audit: Access to raw POC Data is restricted to Provider personnel listed in Appendix A. Any access for troubleshooting must be logged and linked to a ticket.
5. Forensics: Any snapshot beyond the standard retention period requires written authorization and a documented business justification.
6. Deletion/Return: At termination of the POC or upon Customer's written request, Provider will permanently delete raw POC Data and confirm deletion via signed certificate within five (5) business days.
7. Security: Provider will implement encryption-at-rest and in-transit, role-based access control, and object-level auditing for POC Data.
--- End suggested clause ---

Workshop notes & fringe ideas (raw):
- Customer might want escrow escrowed to their own S3 (cross-account). We should offer a signed-role pattern (assume-role) and documented procedure.
- Consider "redaction preview" UI so customer can verify scrubber effectiveness before long-term archive.
- Open question: do we permit model fine-tuning on POC data? default: NO for hosted POCs. Put clause.
- Hard requirement from some banks: no logs outside of their region. Add region-lock option for POC buckets.

Decision register (so SEs know current defaults):
- Default raw retention for hosted POC: 7 days (DECIDED).
- Escrow redacted copy: opt-in, 30 days by default (DECIDED).
- No model training on POC data without explicit invoice-level agreement (DECIDED).

Open questions / Risks:
- How to prove redaction completeness to privacy teams? (suggestion: provide sample redaction report + hash counts).
- Key management: do we allow customer-managed KMS for POC escrow bucket? (legal wants it optional but operational complexity increases).
- Cost: Escrow longer than 30 days will bump pricing; need price appendix for >30/90/365 day options.

Action items (owners & quick due dates):
- [Aisha] Draft customer-facing one-pager summarizing POC retention options (due: 2025-01-16).
- [Jon] Prototype redaction-preview UI mock and handoff to infra (due: 2025-01-24).
- [Priya] Add assume-role cross-account pattern doc to Confluence and sample policy (due: 2025-01-20).
- [Infra] Implement lifecycle policy template and Terraform module for pocs.s3 lifecycle (ticket ENG-2345).

Appendix — Terraform snippets & example lifecycle (high level):
- lifecycle_rule: prefix = "raw/"; expiration_days = 7; noncurrent_version_expiration = 1; abort_incomplete_multipart_upload_days = 2.
- bucket_policy: deny "s3:PutObjectAcl" and require kms:Encrypt.

Notes to legal/GC:
- This doc is intentionally lightweight to accelerate pilots. Provide feedback on minimum language to include for enterprise POCs.
- If customer requires escrow to their own account, legal wants SLA/indemnity language around access and deletion certification.

Quick links & refs:
- SE POC controls index: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SE/POC+Controls+Index
- Telemetry scrub repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry-scrub
- Related ticket: ENG-2193 (POC retention lifecycle)

End of doc.
